_readme: The model ingest manifest. One entry per rigged character.
Everything the captain needed was worked out by hand once — which archive,
which file is the rig, which clip is which, how tall she stands, which maps
to keep and at what size. None of that is character-specific reasoning; it
is the same six questions for every model Meshy or anyone else produces. So
it lives here, and `python tools/ingest_model.py <name>` does the rest.
archive     zip or directory, absolute or relative to the repo root
rig         which file inside it carries the mesh and skeleton to keep.
For Meshy this is an ANIMATION export, not Character_output:
every clip ships its own skeleton and the character file's
rest pose does not match any of them. See DESIGN.md 13f.
clips       our name -> the file that contains that clip
loop        which of those loop; everything else plays once and holds
height      ground units, sole to crown. The renderer scales to this.
maps        albedo/normal/roughness/metallic source patterns and the size
to downscale each to. Meshy ships 4096 albedo and 4096 normal:
56 MB of PNG for a figure 180 pixels tall on screen.
facing      degrees about +Y the rig faces at rest. 0 means it faces +Z.
_boarders: Ready for models. Copy the captain entry, change the archive and the name,
and the renderer picks it up with no code change — it looks for
assets/models/<name>/<name>.tscn where <name> is the enemy kind in lower
case. The kinds are: scrapper, gunner, armored, swarm, boss, crew.
Clips it will use, in the order it falls back: idle, run, swing. Anything
missing degrades — run to walk to idle — so a model with only an idle is
still an improvement on a billboard that never turns.

_note: The first rigged BOARDER (board SG-65, the animation pilot). Meshy's
rigger refused this character in every form it was ever submitted -
twelve 422s across three meshes including two regenerated to the
standing rules (v4 is a verifiably symmetric A-pose with a neck), zero
credits charged - because pose estimation wants humanoid PROPORTION
and a ball with limbs is not that. So the rig is LOCAL:
tools/rig_local.gd builds a Mixamo-named skeleton from measured
landmarks and binds every vertex rigid to its nearest limb, which on a
riveted machine is the honest material. bone_map is empty because the
local rig already speaks Mixamo.
The clip set is the pilot's minimum: walk/run to close the distance,
one swing, a flinch, and idle as the fallback floor (rig3d falls back
to ANY first clip when idle is missing, which is a different bug every
spawn). The captain's baked library carries NO death clip - boarder
deaths stay the sim's despawn until a clip source exists (SG-65 flag).
height 93 = boarder_height(SCRAPPER), the renderer's own arithmetic.
THE FURNACE KNIGHT — the 180-hp wall, the last handoff-3d entry, and the
SECOND rigged boarder. Meshy rejected him twice in July (handoff-3d/
README.md, board SG-22); the owner modelled him himself as the Emberforge
Sentinel and ran the Meshy OBJ through Mixamo's auto-rigger, delivering
the SG-74 shape exactly: one character FBX with skin on native mixamorig_*
bones plus 51 animation-only clips ON THAT RIG. So this is the ARCHIVE
path, one ingest run, and the SG-45 binds/height guards pass BY
CONSTRUCTION — a native rig's Skin binds are born resolving.
The entry is keyed `armored`, not `furnace_knight`, because the renderer
resolves a boarder's mesh from the KIND slug alone (view3d.model_path):
ARMORED -> assets/models/armored/armored.tscn, which is what makes wiring
a boarder a manifest entry rather than a code change. He is the furnace
knight everywhere a human reads the name — the sprite he replaces is
`furnace_knight_front_idle.png` and his sources are archived under
.model_originals/furnace_knight/.
The Mixamo FBX is UNTEXTURED (the OBJ upload was bare), so maps_archive
points at the archived Meshy source and the pipeline re-applies our maps
— the captain/boilerwright precedent. AND THE EMISSION MAP IS LISTED, for
the first time in this manifest: the furnace grille in his chest IS his
identity (the handoff spec asked for exactly one emitter, hot orange,
nothing else), so `ingest_model.gd` learned to read one. Kept at 1024 —
the lit texels are 0.08% of the sheet and a 512 pass costs peak.
height 216 = boarder_height(ARMORED) = (120 + radius*3) with no
FIGURE_SCALE row: the renderer's own arithmetic for this archetype, and
the number the ledger's 'goblins taller than the hero' complaint settled.
He stands a head over the captain's 176, which is the point of him.
Clip names the renderer READS today: idle, walk (his locomotion — a wall
at 75 units a second does not run), run (the fallback tier above it),
swing..swing5 + spin (the VARIANTS rotation — five different two-handed
cuts), hurt (impact -> flinch) and **die**, the first death animation the
game plays. Everything else is aboard under an honest name and listed
UNWIRED on the board row.
Pro Melee Axe Pack: one character FBX with the mesh and skin, and 47
animation-only clips at a fifth of a megabyte each. All 33 bones share
the Mixamo naming and every clip sits a consistent 19.6 degrees off the
character's rest, so one retarget covers the lot. The maps come from the
original Meshy archive because the axe pack's character embeds a 4096
albedo we would only be throwing away.
The second player class, on HIS OWN rig at last. The owner exported the
Meshy mesh (remeshed to ~3000 tris, board SG-12) as an OBJ, ran it
through Mixamo's auto-rigger, and delivered the Great Sword Pack: one
character FBX with skin on native mixamorig_* bones, plus 51
animation-only clips ON THAT SAME RIG — the axe-pack shape exactly
(DESIGN.md 13l), so this entry is the ARCHIVE path again and the old
retarget_library.gd construction (captain clips re-retargeted onto a
bone_map'd Meshy auto-rig) is retired with it. Native rig: the Skin
binds are born resolving (the SG-45 bargain, by construction).
The Mixamo FBX is UNTEXTURED — the OBJ upload was bare — so maps_archive
points at the .model_originals set the Meshy generation left on disk,
and the pipeline re-applies our maps: the captain precedent. The
emission map is there too but ingest_model.gd has no emission reader,
so listing it would be data with no reader; it stays in the originals.
Clip names the renderer READS today: idle/idle_alt, walk, run,
swing..swing5 + spin (the VARIANTS rotation — the wrench swings at
last), dash (Bleed Jet), hurt, plant (Tap Main's kneel, wired through
the clip-stretched-to-window machinery). Everything else is aboard
under an honest name and listed UNWIRED on the board row: strafes,
turns, jumps, kicks, the extra idles/impacts/blocks/crouches, casting,
the draws and the deaths. No run_back in this pack — his backpedal
plays the forward run, recorded, not hidden.
